cards.text: Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles in Babylon (Ezekiel 1:1-3), is in the middle of a vision of Jerusalem's temple. The man clothed in linen has just come back and said, "I have done as You commanded." (Ezekiel 9:11) Now Ezekiel looks up, above the heads of the cherubim, and something is there.

cards.question: Above the heads of the cherubim, Ezekiel sees the likeness of a ___ of sapphire.

cards.text: Then the LORD gives the man in linen a brand new assignment: go inside the wheelwork beneath the cherubim. Friend, my last assignment was "lie in this drawer," and I STILL felt underqualified.

cards.question: Inside the wheelwork beneath the cherubim, what does the LORD tell the man in linen to fill his hands with?
The LORD tells the man in linen to scatter the burning coals over the city.

cards.text: As Ezekiel watches, the man goes in. The cherubim are standing on the south side of the temple, and a cloud fills the inner court.

cards.question: Then the glory of the LORD rises from above the cherubim. Where does it go and stand?

answers.text: over the threshold of the temple
on top of the city wall

cards.question: With the glory of the LORD at the threshold, the temple was filled with the ___, and the court was filled with the ___ of the glory of the LORD.

cards.text: Then the wings of the cherubim start up, and you can hear them all the way out in the outer court. Friend, I can't hear my own oven timer from across the bakery.

cards.question: What does Ezekiel say the sound of the cherubim's wings is like?

answers.text: the voice of God Almighty speaking
a trumpet blast on the mountain

cards.text: The LORD commands the man in linen to take fire from within the wheelwork, from among the cherubim, and the man walks right in and stands beside a wheel. I've worked next to hot ovens my whole life, friend, and I STILL reach for a mitt.

cards.question: The man in linen is standing beside a wheel, and the fire is among the cherubim. Who reaches out and puts the fire into his hands?
After he receives the fire, the man in linen stays inside among the cherubim.

cards.text: Ezekiel adds a little note: the cherubim appear to have the form of human hands under their wings. As somebody who's been using a mustache for hands for years, I fully respect that.
Ezekiel looks again, and now he sees four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub. And these wheels are SHINING.

cards.question: What does Ezekiel say the four wheels beside the cherubim gleam like?
All four of the wheels beside the cherubim have the same form.

cards.text: Each one looks like a wheel within a wheel. And when they move, they can go in any of the four directions.

cards.question: The cherubim and their wheels can go in any of four directions. How do they change direction?

answers.text: they swing around in a circle
they back up and then turn

cards.text: Their whole bodies, backs, hands and wings, are full of eyes all around, and so are their four wheels. Friend, you are NOT sneaking a cookie past them.

cards.question: Ezekiel hears the wheels beside the cherubim being called the ___ wheels.

cards.text: Then come the faces. Each of the cherubim has four of them, and Ezekiel lists them one by one.

cards.question: Each cherub's four faces are a cherub, a man, a lion and one more: the face of the ___.

cards.text: The cherubim rise upward, and it clicks: Ezekiel has seen these living creatures before. Hard to forget a face when there are four of them.

cards.question: Ezekiel recognizes the cherubim. Where had he seen these living creatures before?

cards.text: When the cherubim move, rise or stand still, the wheels do the exact same thing right beside them. I can't get a cookie tray to slide straight, and these wheels never leave their side.

cards.question: Why do the wheels move and rise right along with the cherubim?

answers.text: the spirit of the creatures was in them
the wheels were tied to their wings
the cherubim carried them by hand

cards.text: And now the big moment. The glory of the LORD moves away from the threshold of the temple.

cards.question: The glory of the LORD moves away from the threshold of the temple and stands above the ___.

cards.text: As Ezekiel watches, the cherubim lift their wings and rise up from the ground, with the wheels right beside them. Then they stop.

cards.question: The cherubim rise from the ground with the glory of the LORD above them. Where do they stop?

answers.text: the entrance of the east gate
the Fish Gate by the wall

cards.question: When the cherubim stop at the east gate, the glory of the God of Israel is above them.

cards.text: Ezekiel says it again: these are the living creatures he saw beneath the God of Israel by the River Kebar, and he knew they were cherubim. Each one has four faces, four wings and what looked like human hands under their wings.
Their faces look like the ones he saw by the River Kebar, and each creature goes straight ahead. Hold on to your apron, friend, because this vision isn't finished yet.
